body.text: Ratnākaraśānti: Bhramaharanāma Hevajrasādhana
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>: The <s>Hevajra Sādhana</s> (practice) Named 'Dispeller of Confusion'

children.translated_text: With the ocean hurled about by the force of the earth bowed under the weight of his footsteps,
emitting sounds from faces resembling the clouds of cosmic dissolution,
the ridges of mountains shattered by the wind of the forest of his arms—
may the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (cosmic dance) of <s>Heruka</s> remove your fear!
I compose a <s>sādhana</s> (practice) for each face of the eight-faced, three-eyed one,
of <s>Hevajra</s>, who moves on four feet and has sixteen arms.

body.text: iha bhāvanādhikṛto mantrī prātar utthāya hṛdayārkanyastanijabījaḥ kṛtamukhaśaucādiḥ
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) authorized for <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), having risen in the morning, having placed his own seed-syllable upon the sun at his heart, and having performed cleansing of the mouth and so forth,

body.text: oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā
body.translated_text: Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā

body.text: iti sthānātmayogarakṣāṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpādisurabhitāṃ dhyānabhūmiṃ praviśya, sukhāsane paryaṅkam ābhujya, arghaṃ parijapya, hṛnmantrakiraṇākṛṣṭam abhimukham ākāśe saparivāraṃ bhagavantam avalokya, hṛdbījanirgatābhir gauryādidevībhir aṣṭābhiḥ pūjayet. tatra gaurī śaśinaṃ bibharti, caurī raviṃ, vettālī jalam, ghasmarī palalam, pukkasī candanam, śabarī madhu, caṇḍālī ḍamarukaṃ vādayati, ḍombī kaṇṭhalagnā puruṣāyate. tatas tasyaiva bhagavato 'grataḥ pāpadeśanādikam iti kuryāt -
body.translated_text: having thus performed the protection of the yoga of self and place, entering the meditation ground made fragrant with incense, flowers, and so forth, sitting cross-legged on a comfortable seat, having recited over the water offering, beholding the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) face-to-face in the sky together with his retinue, drawn by the rays of the heart-<s>mantra</s>, one should worship with the eight goddesses beginning with <s>Gaurī</s>, who have emerged from the heart seed-syllable. There, <s>Gaurī</s> holds the moon, <s>Caurī</s> the sun, <s>Vettālī</s> water, <s>Ghasmarī</s> flesh, <s>Pukkasī</s> sandalwood, <s>Śabarī</s> honey, <s>Caṇḍālī</s> plays the <s>ḍamaru</s> (drum), and <s>Ḍombī</s>, clinging to his neck, acts as the male partner. Then, before that very <s>Bhagavān</s>, one should perform confession of sins and so forth as follows:

body.text: sarvam ātmanaḥ pāpaṃ bhagavataḥ purataḥ pratideśayāmi, sarvabuddhabodhisattvāryapṛthagjanānāṃ sarvakuśalam anumode, sarvaṃ cātmanaḥ kuśalam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayāmi. eṣo 'ham ā bodher buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānām agryam. dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi samagraṃ mahāyānam. saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmy avaivartikabodhisattvagaṇam. aho batāham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ abhisaṃbudheya sarvasattvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya yāvad atyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe buddhabodhau pratiṣṭhāpanāya. eṣo 'ham anuttaraṃ bodhimārgam āśrayāmi yad uta vajrayānam.
body.translated_text: I confess all my sins before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. I rejoice in all the merit of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, Noble Ones, and ordinary beings. I dedicate all my own merit toward unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> until enlightenment, the foremost among bipeds. I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>, the complete <s>Mahāyāna</s>. I go for refuge to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the assembly of irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Oh, may I awaken to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings, in order to establish them in the ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. I take refuge in the unsurpassed path to enlightenment, namely the <s>Vajrayāna</s>.

body.text: tataḥ sarvasattveṣu divyasukhopasaṃhārākārāṃ maitrīm, sarvaduḥkhāpanayanākārāṃ karuṇām, divyasukhāviyoganiyamākārāṃ muditām, kleśapratipakṣamārgopasaṃhārākārām upekṣāṃ ca bhāvayet. tataḥ sarvadharmān manasālambya vicārayet ḥ cittam evaitat tena tenākāreṇa bhrāntaṃ pratibhāsate yathāsvapne.
body.translated_text: Then one should cultivate <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings in the form of bringing divine happiness, <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) in the form of removing all suffering, <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) in the form of the commitment to non-separation from divine happiness, and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) in the form of applying the path as antidote to afflictions. Then, taking all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) as objects of mind, one should contemplate: It is mind alone that, confused in various ways, appears thus, just as in a dream.

body.text: nāsti cittād bāhyaṃ cittagrāhyam. grāhyābhāvāc cittam api grāhakaṃ na bhavati. tasmāc cittaśarīrāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, teṣāṃ grāhyagrāhakaśūnyatā paramārtha iti. evam ekāntena niścitya bhrāntisamāropitaṃ bhrānticihnaṃ sarvadharmāṇām ākāraṃ vihāya teṣāṃ prakṛtim eva kevalām advayavijñaptilakṣaṇāṃ śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśāṃ śaradamalamadhyāhnagaganopamām anantāṃ paśyet. idam ucyate pāramārthikaṃ bodhicittaṃ lokottaraṃ śūnyatājñānaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ nirvikalpam. tatas tan mantreṇādhitiṣṭhet
body.translated_text: There is nothing external to mind that is apprehended by mind. Due to the absence of the apprehended, mind too is not an apprehender. Therefore all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) have mind as their body; their emptiness of apprehended and apprehender is the <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality). Having thus ascertained with certainty, abandoning the form of all <s>dharmas</s> that is the mark of confusion superimposed by confusion, one should see their nature alone—characterized by non-dual cognition, resembling pure crystal, like the stainless autumn midday sky, infinite. This is called the ultimate <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind), the supramundane <s>śūnyatā-jñāna</s> (emptiness-knowledge), free from elaboration, free from conceptualization. Then one should consecrate it with this <s>mantra</s>:

body.text: oṃ śūnyatājñānavajrasvabhāvātmako 'ham.
body.translated_text: Oṃ, I am of the nature whose essence is the <s>vajra</s> of <s>śūnyatā-jñāna</s> (emptiness-knowledge).

body.text: saiva bhagavatī prajñāpāramitā, saiva paramā rakṣā.
body.translated_text: That itself is the Blessed <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom); that itself is the supreme protection.

body.text: tatas tanniṣyandabhūtām ākāravatīṃ rakṣāṃ śuddhalaukikajñānasvabhāvāṃ bhāvayet.
body.translated_text: Then one should meditate on the protection that has form, which is the outflow of that [emptiness], having the nature of pure mundane knowledge.

children.text: repheṇa sūryaṃ purato vibhāvya tasmin ravau hūṃbhavaviśvavajram /
children.translated_text: Having visualized a sun before oneself by means of the syllable RE, upon that sun a <s>viśvavajra</s> (double vajra) born from HŪṂ,

children.text: tenaiva vajreṇa vibhāvayec ca prākārakaṃ pañjarabandhanaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: with that very <s>vajra</s> one should visualize both a surrounding wall and a cage-enclosure.

body.text: viśvavajrakiraṇaiḥ pralayānaladuḥsahaiḥ sarvataḥ spharitvā
body.translated_text: Having pervaded all directions with the rays of the <s>viśvavajra</s>, unbearable like the fire of cosmic dissolution,

body.text: ghanībhūya racitaṃ tiryak caturasraṃjvaladvajraprākāram, upariṣṭād vajrapañjaram, adhastād vajramayīṃ bhūmim ārasātalaviracitāṃ paśyet. tato raviviśvavajrābhyāṃ raśmībhūya diśi diśi spharitvā ghanībhūya bahir dūre sīmābandhaḥ karaṇīya iti ślokārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: having become dense, one should see a square blazing <s>vajra</s> wall formed horizontally, above a <s>vajra</s> cage, and below a <s>vajra</s> ground constructed down to <s>Rasātala</s> (the netherworld). Then, from the sun and <s>viśvavajra</s>, having become rays and having pervaded in every direction, having become dense, the boundary protection should be made far outside—this is the meaning of the verse.

body.text: tatas tanniṣyandatayaiva viśuddhāni pañca mahābhūtāni cintayet. tatrākāśamahābhūtaṃ dharmodayākhyaṃ mahāvajradharasvabhāvaṃ śaracchaśadharadhavalam adhaḥ sūkṣmam upari viśālaṃ trikoṇam antar gaganasvarūpaṃ abhyantarodgataviśvadaIakamalakarṇikāvasthitavipulaviśvavajram. tadvedikāyāṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni caturmaṇḍalākārāṇi caturdevīsvabhāvāny upary upari paśyet. ādau laṃkāreṇa māhendramaṇḍalaṃ caturasraṃ pītaṃ koṇeṣu triśūkavajrāṅkam. tato vaṃkāreṇa vāruṇaṃ vartulaṃ sitaṃ ghaṭāṅkam. tato raṃkāreṇāgneyaṃ trikoṇaṃ raktaṃ koṇeṣu rephāṅkam. tato yaṃkāreṇa vāyavyaṃ dhanurākāraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ koṭidvaye calatpatākāṅkam. bhāvakas tu tadānīṃ tad eva lokottarajñānaṃ
body.translated_text: Then one should contemplate the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) as purified, being of the very nature of that [wisdom's] outflow. Among these, the <s>ākāśa-mahābhūta</s> (space element), called <s>dharmodaya</s> (source of dharma), having the nature of great <s>Vajradhara</s>, white as the autumn moon, narrow below and broad above, triangular, with the inner nature of open sky, and within it a great <s>viśvavajra</s> (universal vajra) situated on the pericarp of a <s>viśvadala</s> lotus emerging from within. On its platform, one should see the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) in the form of four <s>maṇḍalas</s>, having the nature of four goddesses, one above another. First, from the syllable LAṂ, the <s>māhendra-maṇḍala</s> (earth maṇḍala), square, yellow, marked with three-pronged vajras at the corners. Then, from the syllable VAṂ, the <s>vāruṇa</s> (water maṇḍala), circular, white, marked with a pot. Then, from the syllable RAṂ, the <s>āgneya</s> (fire maṇḍala), triangular, red, marked with the syllable RE at the corners. Then, from the syllable YAṂ, the <s>vāyavya</s> (wind maṇḍala), bow-shaped, black, marked with waving banners at both ends. The practitioner at that time is that very supramundane wisdom

body.text: vyāpakatvena sthitam. tato viśvavajravedikāmadhye caturmahābhūtapariṇāmajaṃ pariśuddhabuddhakṣetrasaṃkṣeparūpaṃ mahāmokṣapuraṃ vairocanasvabhāvaṃ nānāratnamayaṃ kūṭāgāram aṣṭābhiḥ śmaśānaiḥ sarvalokadhātunairātmyasūcakaiḥ parivṛtaṃ dhyāyāt.
body.translated_text: abiding in a pervading manner. Then, in the middle of the <s>viśvavajra</s> platform, one should meditate on the great liberation-city (<s>mahāmokṣapura</s>), born from the transformation of the four great elements, having the form of a condensed pure <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), with the nature of <s>Vairocana</s>, made of various jewels — a peaked pavilion (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>) surrounded by eight charnel grounds (<s>śmaśāna</s>) indicating the selflessness of all world-realms.

children.translated_text: Square, with four doors, adorned with eight pillars,
Surrounded by four platforms, decorated with four archways,
With necklaces, half-necklaces, silk-garlands, festoons, canopies, mirrors, and fly-whisks,
Beautiful, with <s>vajra</s>-strings, and radiant with a flood of Buddha-rays,
With directions made resonant by bells at the tips of waving colorful banners,

children.text: paramaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmair upahāraiś ca harṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: And delighting with the supreme five objects of desire and with offerings.
In its inner chamber, a lotus with eight petals and filaments,
With seats at the four doors, four corners, and the pericarp.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>; and <s>Yama</s>, the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>,
<s>Nairṛti</s>, and <s>Vemacitri</s>; and in the center, the four <s>Māras</s>.
The four <s>Māras</s>, each more supine than the last, facing upward, terrified,
Their hearts trampled by the sun, and the others cowering under the moon.

body.text: tatra madhyāsanasyopari pañcadaśabhiḥ svaraiś candramaṇḍalam ādarśajñānasvabhāvam, tadupari catustriṃśadvyañjanaiḥ sūryamaṇḍalaṃ samatājñānasvabhāvam, tanmadhye aṃkārahūṃkārapariṇatau
body.translated_text: There, above the central seat, a moon <s>maṇḍala</s> [formed] from the fifteen vowels, having the nature of <s>ādarśajñāna</s> (mirror-like wisdom); above that, a sun <s>maṇḍala</s> [formed] from the thirty-four consonants, having the nature of <s>samatājñāna</s> (equality wisdom); in its center, one should contemplate

body.text: karttikapālau saṃyuktau svabījamadhyagatau pratyavekṣaṇājñānātmakau cintayet. tato bījadvayād yoginīcakrākāreṇa sarvatathāgatān saṃsphārya, tān saṃhṛtya, taiḥ sahaikīkṛtaṃ bījaṃ kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānam, tataś candrasūryacihnabījapariṇāmajaṃ bhagavantaṃ vajrasattvaṃ vakṣyamāṇavarṇākṛticihnādinā śrīherukarūpeṇāvirbhūtaṃ tathaiva nairātmyāśliṣṭakandharaṃ suviśuddhadharmadhātujñānātmakaṃ paśyet. iti pañcākārābhisaṃbodhiḥ.
body.translated_text: a <s>karttī</s> (curved knife) and <s>kapāla</s> (skull-cup) — transformed from AṂ and HŪṂ — conjoined, situated within the seed-syllable, having the nature of <s>pratyavekṣaṇājñāna</s> (discriminating wisdom). Then, from the pair of seed-syllables, having emanated all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the form of a <s>yoginī-cakra</s>, and having withdrawn them, the seed unified with them becomes <s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s> (all-accomplishing wisdom). Then one should see the Blessed <s>Vajrasattva</s>, born from the transformation of the moon, sun, signs, and seed-syllable, appearing in the form of glorious <s>Heruka</s> with the colors, shapes, signs, and other attributes to be described, embraced around the neck by <s>Nairātmyā</s>, having the nature of the completely pure <s>dharmadhātujñāna</s> (wisdom of the dharma-realm). This is the <s>pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi</s> (five-aspect awakening).

children.translated_text: From the mouth of that blissful one, intertwined with two HŪṂ syllables,

children.text: jvalad bījadvayaṃ rāgāt padmāntaḥ praviśad dravet //
children.translated_text: The blazing pair of seed-syllables, melting from passion, enters into the lotus and dissolves.

children.text: tato vajrī mahārāgād vilīya saha vidyayā /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>vajrī</s> (vajra-holder), from great passion, having melted together with the <s>vidyā</s> (consort),
Remains in the state of a <s>maṇḍala</s>, resembling the molten autumn moon.
Then, for his arising, the goddesses, standing on the corner-seats and moon[-seats],
Should urge [him] — four [goddesses] with four <s>vajragītis</s> (vajra songs):

body.text: uṭṭha bharāḍo karuṇamaṇu pukkasi mahuṃ paritāhi /
body.translated_text: [<s>Pukkasī</s>:] 'Arise, O lord! Compassionate one, protect me, <s>Pukkasī</s>!'

body.text: mahasuhajoeṃ kāma mahuṃ cchaḍḍahi suṇṇasamāhi //
body.translated_text: 'Abandon the great bliss, O lover! Abandon the meditation on emptiness for me!'

children.text: tojjha vihuṇṇe marami haüṃ uṭṭhahi tuhuṃ hevajja /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śabarī</s>:] 'Without you I die, stripped bare! Arise, O <s>Hevajra</s>!'
'Abandon the nature of emptiness! O <s>Śabarī</s>, let the task be accomplished!'

children.text: loa nimantia suraapahu suṇṇe acchasi kīsa /
children.translated_text: [<s>Caṇḍālī</s>:] 'Invited by the world, O lord of gods, why do you remain in emptiness?'

children.text: haüṃ caṇḍālī viṇṇamami taï viṇu uhami na dīsa //
children.translated_text: 'I, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, implore you — without you, I see no direction!'

children.text: indīālī uṭṭha tuhuṃ haüṃ jāṇami tuhu citta /
children.translated_text: [<s>Ḍombī</s>:] 'O <s>Indīālī</s>, arise! I know your mind.'

children.text: aṃhe ḍombī cchea maṇu mā karu karuṇavicchitta //
children.translated_text: 'We are <s>Ḍombī</s> — abandon your thought! Do not sever your compassion!'

body.text: atha gītikānurodhāc candradravasaṃhārajābhyāṃ tatkālajaravimaṇḍalasthitābhyām aṃkārahūṃkārābhyāṃ devatānāṃ cihnadehādikam ākāśopamaṃ māyopamaṃ ca niścitya, tatpariṇāmayoḥ karttikapālayoḥ saṃyuktayor dṛḍhasamādhirūpayor garbhe tad eva
body.translated_text: Then, urged by the songs, having determined that the sign-bodies and other aspects of the deities — born from the withdrawal of the moon-drops and situated on the contemporary sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> from the AṂ and HŪṂ syllables — are like space and like illusion, then from the transformation of those two, the <s>karttī</s> and <s>kapāla</s> conjoined, being of the nature of firm <s>samādhi</s>, within their womb that very

body.text: bījadvayaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānasvabhāvaṃ paśyet. tata eva spharaṇayogena yoginīcakrākārānantatathāgatamayaṃ cittādhīnaṃ ca viśvaṃ nirūpya saṃharaṇayogena sarvaṃ tan māyopamaṃ gaganopamaṃ ca parijñāya dvitīyaravicihnabījapariṇāmajaṃ śrīherukam ātmānaṃ paśyet.
body.translated_text: one should see the pair of seed syllables as having the nature of knowledge of things as they truly are. Then, by the yoga of emanation, having determined the universe to be of the nature of infinite <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the form of a <s>yoginī-cakra</s> and subject to the mind, and by the yoga of withdrawal, having understood all that to be like an illusion and like space, one should see oneself as the glorious <s>Heruka</s>, born from the transformation of the seed syllable marked with the second ray.

children.translated_text: Stamping his feet, threatening the gods and demons,
wrathful, with round red eyes, graceful, in the bloom of youth,
with four feet, eight faces, adorned with twice-eight arms,
having trampled the four <s>Māras</s>, dancing in <s>ardhaparyaṅka</s> (half-cross-legged) posture,
wearing a great necklace of severed heads, standing on the sun, terrifying and frightful,
bearing the <s>viśvavajra</s> (double vajra) on his crown, black, with a radiance blazing like the sun,
his face resounding with the syllable <s>HŪṂ</s>, his body smeared with ashes,
the principal face deep black, the right one white like a jasmine flower,
the left one red and most terrific, the top face fierce and horrifying,
the remaining faces dark as a bee, each face with three eyes,
endowed with the nine dramatic sentiments (<s>navarasa</s>): the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), heroic (<s>vīra</s>), disgusting (<s>bībhatsa</s>),
furious (<s>raudra</s>), comic (<s>hāsya</s>), fearsome (<s>bhayānaka</s>), compassionate (<s>karuṇā</s>), wondrous (<s>adbhuta</s>), and peaceful (<s>śānta</s>),
with tawny upward-streaming hair, adorned with the five <s>mudrās</s> (seals):

children.text: cakrī kuṇḍala kaṇṭhā ca haste rucaka mekhalam //
children.translated_text: the wheel (<s>cakrī</s>), earrings (<s>kuṇḍala</s>), necklace (<s>kaṇṭhā</s>), bracelets (<s>rucaka</s>) on the hands, and girdle (<s>mekhala</s>).
Elephant, horse, donkey, cow, camel, human, <s>śarabha</s> (mythical beast), and cat —
in the eight skull-cups of the right [hands], these bipeds and quadrupeds should be known in order.

children.text: pṛthivī varuṇa vāyuś ca tejaś candrārka eva ca /
children.translated_text: Earth, <s>Varuṇa</s> (water), wind, fire, moon, sun,
<s>Antaka</s> (god of death), and <s>Dhanada</s> (lord of wealth) — these are in the eight skull-cups of the left [hands].
He is embraced by <s>Nairātmyā</s>, [adorned] with her own five <s>mudrās</s>,
two-armed, one-faced, two-legged, she holding a <s>karttī</s> (curved knife) and a skull-cup.

body.text: atha bhagavato hṛtsūryasthitakapālasūrye hūṃkāram, bhagavatyās tu hṛccandrasthitakarttimuṣṭicandre aṃkāraṃ cintayet. tato 'sya śrotre nairātmyām, cakṣuṣi vajrām, ghrāṇe guhyagaurīm,
body.translated_text: Then one should visualize in the sun situated in the skull-cup at the Blessed One's heart the syllable <s>HŪṂ</s>, and in the moon situated in the fist holding the <s>karttī</s> at the Blessed Lady's heart the syllable <s>AṂ</s>. Then one should place in his ears <s>Nairātmyā</s>, in his eyes <s>Vajrā</s>, in his nose <s>Guhyagaurī</s>,

body.text: jihvāyāṃ vāriyoginīm, kāyendriye vajraḍākīm, manasi nairātmyām adhimuñcet. etad eva vajrādipañcakaṃ yathākramaṃ rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaskandheṣu, tathā mohamātsaryarāgerṣyādveṣeṣu. rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmāyataneṣu bāhyagaurī caurī vettālī ghasmarī bhūcarī khecarī, pṛthivyaptejovāyudhātuṣu pukkasī śabarī caṇḍālī ḍombī, kāyavākcitteṣu bhūcarīkhecarīnairātmyāḥ, māṃse pukkasī, rudhire śabarī, śukre caṇḍālī, majjamedayor ḍombī, carmaṇi sapta bodhyaṅgāni, asthiṣu satyacatuṣṭayam. evaṃ devatābhiḥ sakalīkṛtya tadaparāḥ śuddhīr adhimuñcet.
body.translated_text: on his tongue <s>Vāriyoginī</s>, in his body-faculty <s>Vajraḍākī</s>, and in his mind <s>Nairātmyā</s>. This very group of five beginning with <s>Vajrā</s> should be placed in order in the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; likewise in delusion, envy, passion, jealousy, and hatred; in the external <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharma</s> — <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Caurī</s>, <s>Vettālī</s>, <s>Ghasmarī</s>, <s>Bhūcarī</s>, <s>Khecarī</s>; in the elements of earth, water, fire, and wind — <s>Pukkasī</s>, <s>Śabarī</s>, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, <s>Ḍombī</s>; in body, speech, and mind — <s>Bhūcarī</s>, <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Nairātmyā</s>; in flesh <s>Pukkasī</s>, in blood <s>Śabarī</s>, in semen <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, in marrow and fat <s>Ḍombī</s>; in skin the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), in bones the four noble truths (<s>satyacatuṣṭaya</s>). Having thus integrated [all] with the deities, one should apply the remaining purifications.

children.translated_text: The eyes are red through compassion; the body is black through the mind of loving-kindness;
the feet are the four means of gathering [disciples]; the sixteen arms are the sixteen [types of] emptiness.

children.text: mukhāny aṣṭau vimokṣās tu tribhis tattvais trilocanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eight faces are the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>); with three realities he is three-eyed;

children.text: pañca mudrā jināḥ pañca kruddho duṣṭānuśāsanam //
children.translated_text: the five <s>mudrās</s> (seals) are the five <s>Jinas</s> (victorious Buddhas); his wrath is the discipline of the wicked.

body.text: kaṇṭhahṛdbhagamasteṣu catuścakraṃ yathākramam /
body.translated_text: At the throat, heart, genitals, and crown, the four <s>cakras</s> (circles) in order

body.text: saṃbhogadharmanirmāṇamahāsukham iti smṛtam //
body.translated_text: are remembered as <s>Saṃbhoga</s> (enjoyment), <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Nirmāṇa</s> (emanation), and <s>Mahāsukha</s> (great bliss).

children.translated_text: Lotuses with sixteen, eight, four and sixty, and thirty-two petals,
adorned in the center with the syllables <s>OṂ</s>, <s>HŪṂ</s>, <s>Ā</s>, and <s>HAṂ</s>.

body.text: tadanu svahṛdbījaraśmispharaṇāṅkuśair daśadiggatāṃs tathāgatān ākṛṣya nabhasi saṃsthāpya tān aṣṭamātṛbhiḥ saṃpūjya
body.translated_text: Then, having drawn the <s>Tathāgatas</s> dwelling in the ten directions with hooks of rays emanating from the seed syllable at one's own heart, establishing them in space, and worshipping them with the eight <s>Mātṛs</s> (mothers),

body.text: abhiṣiñcantu māṃ sarvatathāgatāḥ
body.translated_text: 'May all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> consecrate me!' —

body.text: iti prārthayet. taiḥ śrīherukarūpāpannaiḥ pañcāmṛtabhṛtapañcatathāgatātmakaiḥ kalaśair abhiṣicyate. abhiṣicyamānasya śirasi bhagavān akṣobhya utpadyate, puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ kuṅkumavṛṣṭiś ca bhavati, dundubhiśabdaś ca śrūyate, rūpavajrādibhiḥ saṃpūjyate, vajragītyā locanādibhiḥ stūyate.
body.translated_text: thus one should pray. By them, who have assumed the form of the glorious <s>Heruka</s>, one is consecrated with vessels filled with the five nectars, having the essence of the five <s>Tathāgatas</s>. As one is being consecrated, the Blessed One <s>Akṣobhya</s> appears at one's crown; a rain of flowers and a rain of saffron fall; the sound of kettledrums is heard; one is worshipped by <s>Rūpavajrā</s> and the others; and one is praised in the <s>Vajra</s> song by <s>Locanā</s> and the others.

body.text: ity ādiyogo nāma samādhiḥ, svābhāvikaś ca kāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Thus is the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called the 'initial yoga,' and this is the <s>svābhāvikakāya</s> (natural body).

body.text: atha padmādhiṣṭhānam.
body.translated_text: Now, the consecration of the lotus (<s>padmādhiṣṭhāna</s>):

children.translated_text: <s>OṂ</s> Lotus, support of bliss, great passion, bestower of bliss,

children.text: caturānandabhāg viśva hūṃ hūṃ kāryaṃ kuruṣva me //
children.translated_text: partaker of the four joys, all-pervading — <s>HŪṂ HŪṂ</s>, accomplish this act for me!

body.text: atha vajrādhiṣṭhānam.
body.translated_text: Now, the consecration of the <s>vajra</s> (<s>vajrādhiṣṭhāna</s>):

children.translated_text: <s>OṂ Vajra</s>, great wrath, bestower of the four joys —

children.text: khagamukhaikaraso nātha hūṃ hūṃ kāryaṃ kuruṣva me //
children.translated_text: O lord, of one taste with the sky-faced ones (<s>khaganmukhā</s>), HŪṂ HŪṂ, accomplish the task for me!

body.text: tataḥ
body.translated_text: Then,

body.text: oṃ śī 3 ha 3 svāhā
body.translated_text: OṂ ŚĪ ŚĪ ŚĪ HA HA HA SVĀHĀ

body.text: iti ratim ārabhet. tataḥ kamalodarapatitacandradravabindupariṇāmena gaṃkāreṇa niṣpannāṃ gaurīṃ kṛṣṇavarṇāṃ karttirohitadharāṃ pūrvadvārāsanacandre cintayet. tathā caṃkāreṇa caurīṃ māñjiṣṭhavarṇāṃ kṛpīṭaśūkaradharāṃ dakṣiṇadvārāsanacandre, tathā vaṃkāreṇa vettālīṃ kanakavarṇāṃ kūrmakapāladharāṃ paścimadvārāsanacandre, tathā ghaṃkāreṇa ghasmarīṃ maraktābhām. bhujagayogapātrīdharām uttaradvārāsanacandre, tathā paṃkāreṇa pukkasīm indranīlanibhāṃ keśariparśudharāṃ aiśānakoṇāsanacandre, tathā śaṃkāreṇa śabarīṃ candrakāntanibhāṃ bhikṣukhikkhirikādharām āgneyakoṇāsanacandre,
body.translated_text: one should begin the sexual union (<s>rati</s>). Then, through the transformation of the drop of moon-liquid fallen into the interior of the lotus, by the syllable GAṂ one should visualize the generated <s>Gaurī</s>, black in color, holding a knife (<s>kartri</s>) and a red fish (<s>rohita</s>), on the moon-seat at the eastern door. Likewise, by the syllable CAṂ, <s>Caurī</s>, madder-red in color, holding a skull-cup (<s>kṛpīṭa</s>) and a pig (<s>śūkara</s>), on the moon-seat at the southern door. Likewise, by VAṂ, <s>Vettālī</s>, golden in color, holding a tortoise (<s>kūrma</s>) and a skull-bowl (<s>kapāla</s>), on the moon-seat at the western door. Likewise, by GHAṂ, <s>Ghasmarī</s>, emerald-like in appearance, holding a serpent (<s>bhujaga</s>) and a ritual vessel (<s>yogapātrī</s>), on the moon-seat at the northern door. Likewise, by PAṂ, <s>Pukkasī</s>, sapphire-like in appearance, holding a lion (<s>keśarī</s>) and an axe (<s>paraśu</s>), on the moon-seat at the northeastern (<s>Aiśāna</s>) corner. Likewise, by ŚAṂ, <s>Śabarī</s>, moonstone-like in appearance, holding a monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>) and a rattle (<s>khikkhirikā</s>), on the moon-seat at the southeastern (<s>Āgneya</s>) corner.

body.text: tathā laṃkāreṇa caṇḍālīṃ nabhaḥśyāmāṃ cakralāṅgaladharāṃ naiṛtikoṇāsanacandre, tathā ḍaṃkāreṇa ḍombīṃ karburavarṇāṃ vajratarjanikādharāṃ vāyavyakoṇāsanacandre dhyāyāt.
body.translated_text: Likewise, by LAṂ, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, dark as the sky, holding a wheel (<s>cakra</s>) and a plow (<s>lāṅgala</s>), on the moon-seat at the southwestern (<s>Nairṛti</s>) corner. Likewise, by ḌAṂ, <s>Ḍombī</s>, variegated in color, holding a <s>vajra</s> and a threatening finger (<s>tarjanī</s>), on the moon-seat at the northwestern (<s>Vāyavya</s>) corner — one should meditate [on all of them].

children.translated_text: Standing in <s>ardhaparyaṅka</s> (half-seated) dance posture, round, red, three-eyed,
with tawny upward-standing hair, two-armed, bearing the five <s>mudrās</s> — such are they.

body.text: atha parito niṣpannaṃ maṇḍalam avalokya hṛdbījakiraṇāṅkuśair jñānamaṇḍalam ākṛṣya, pūrvadvārābhimukham antarīkṣe 'vasthāpya, aṣṭānanahūṃkārair vighnān utsārya, arghapādyaṃ dattvā,
body.translated_text: Then, having observed the <s>maṇḍala</s> completely generated around, with ray-hooks from the heart-seed syllable, one draws in the <s>jñānamaṇḍala</s> (wisdom-maṇḍala), places it in the sky facing the eastern door, expels obstacles with eight ANA-HŪṂ syllables, offers <s>arghya</s> (water-offering) and <s>pādya</s> (foot-water),

body.text: jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ
body.translated_text: JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ

body.text: ity ebhir yathākramam ākarṣaṇapraveśanabandhanavaśīkaraṇāni kṛtvā, samayajñānamaṇḍalayor ekalolībhāvaṃ vibhāvya, hṛnmantrakiraṇaiḥ sarvatathāgatān ākṛṣya saṃpūjya prārthya tayor abhiṣekaṃ dāpayet. abhiṣicyamānānām abhiṣekajinaḥ śirasi jāyate. atra ślokau:
body.translated_text: With these, performing respectively attraction (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>), entering (<s>praveśana</s>), binding (<s>bandhana</s>), and subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>), having visualized the merging into oneness of the <s>samaya</s> and <s>jñāna</s> <s>maṇḍalas</s>, with heart-<s>mantra</s> rays drawing in all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, worshipping them, requesting them, one should cause them to confer <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration). For those being consecrated, the consecration-<s>Jina</s> appears on the head. Here are two verses:

children.text: pukkasyādyāś catasras tu gauryādyāś ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: The four beginning with <s>Pukkasī</s>, and those beginning with <s>Gaurī</s>, in due order,
should be sealed here by <s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Buddharatneśa</s>, and <s>Vāgīśa</s>.

body.text: kuleśaiḥ kāyavākcittair bhavanirvāṇaherukān /
body.translated_text: The <s>Herukas</s> of existence (<s>bhava</s>) and <s>nirvāṇa</s> [should be sealed] by the family lords (<s>kuleśas</s>) of body, speech, and mind;

body.text: vajrādyāḥ svakuleśais tu jinair akṣobhyapañcakaiḥ //
body.translated_text: the <s>Vajra</s> [deities] and others by their own family lords, the <s>Jinas</s> of the fivefold <s>Akṣobhya</s> group.

body.text: tato devatātattvaṃ manasikuryāt. iha sarvadharmāḥ kāyavākcittajñānaiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ. teṣāṃ kāyādīnāṃ yā dharmatā vijñaptimātratā dvayaśūnyatā tasyāḥ pratyavekṣaṇaṃ yathāyogaṃ dvārapālīnāṃ tattvam. tasyā eva śūnyatāyāḥ samyagjñānaṃ niṣprapañcam anāsravā prajñā vajrayānam anuttaraṃ yathāyogaṃ pukkasyādīnāṃ catasṛṇāṃ tattvam. tasyaiva vajrayānasya phalaṃ mahāvajradharapadaṃ niruttarā bodhir maṇḍalādhipates tattvam.
body.translated_text: Then one should contemplate the reality of the deity (<s>devatātattva</s>). Here, all <s>dharmas</s> are encompassed by body, speech, mind, and <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom). The <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of body and the rest — which is <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (consciousness-only) and <s>dvayaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of duality) — its investigation is the reality of the door-protectresses, as appropriate. The correct knowledge of that very emptiness, free from elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), the undefiled wisdom (<s>anāsravā prajñā</s>), the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s> — is the reality of the four <s>Pukkasī</s> and the rest, as appropriate. The fruit of that very <s>Vajrayāna</s>, the state of <s>Mahāvajradhara</s>, unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), is the reality of the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: tataḥ svahṛdbījād aṣṭau pūjādevīḥ saṃsphārya tāsāṃ spharaṇameghair gaganam āpūrya sanāyakaṃ maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet. tato māyopamān sarvadharmān adhimucya gītidvayena bhagavantaṃ stūyāt.
body.translated_text: Then, from one's heart-seed, emanating eight offering goddesses (<s>pūjādevīs</s>), filling the sky with their emanation-clouds, one should worship the <s>maṇḍala</s> together with its lord. Then, having resolved all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion-like (<s>māyopama</s>), one should praise the <s>Bhagavān</s> with two songs.

body.text:
vividhavicitravibhramālokitaiḥ pramodya
vividhavicitracumbanāliṅganaiḥ pramodya /
body.translated_text:
With varied and wondrous glances of play, delighting;
with varied and wondrous kisses and embraces, delighting;

body.text:
vividhavicitrasukhabhojanaiḥ prabhakṣya
vividhavicitrasaṃvaram aho pradarśayasva //
body.translated_text:
with varied and wondrous feasts of pleasure, devouring —
the varied and wondrous <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint), ah, reveal it!

children.translated_text: Enter equally into all beings;
consume everything, dissolve into all beings.

body.text: athāntarīkṣe hūṃkāreṇa vajraṃ vicintya, tasyādhastād āḥkāreṇa padmam, tanmadhye praṇavāṅkitāni dravyāṇi, vajrapadmasamāyogād agnijvālanam, tena teṣāṃ tāpanam, pākād dravīkṛtya jñānasūryīkaraṇād dyotanam, tatkiraṇair daśadiksarvatathāgatānāṃ rūpadarśanam, tajjñānabījebhyas tair eva kiraṇair ākṛṣya jñānāmṛtaṃ teṣu saṃpātya samarasīkuryāt. evaṃ tāny amṛtīkṛtya tryakṣareṇādhiṣṭhāya hūṃkāreṇa jihvāyāṃ śubhravajram, hṛtsūrye ca maṇḍalam adhimucya, tair amṛtair ātmānaṃ maṇḍalaṃ ca saṃtarpayet.
body.translated_text: Then, in the sky, one should visualize a <s>vajra</s> from the syllable HŪṂ, beneath it a lotus from ĀḤ, within it substances marked with <s>praṇava</s> (OṂ). From the union of <s>vajra</s> and lotus, fire blazes, heating those [substances]. Through cooking, they are melted; through making them the sun of <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom), they are illuminated. With those rays, one sees all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions. From their <s>jñāna</s>-seeds, with those very rays, drawing in the <s>jñānāmṛta</s> (wisdom-nectar), causing it to fall into those [substances], one should make them of one taste (<s>samarasa</s>). Having thus transformed them into <s>amṛta</s>, consecrating with the three syllables, [placing] on the tongue from HŪṂ a white <s>vajra</s>, and on the heart-sun the <s>maṇḍala</s>, with that <s>amṛta</s> one should satisfy oneself and the <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: mātṛcakre pure ramye bhāvayed īdṛśaṃ prabhum /
children.translated_text: In the charming city of the <s>mātṛcakra</s> (mothers' circle), one should meditate on such a lord,
one who has attained waveless bliss, whose very nature is waveless.

body.text: iti maṇḍalarājāgrī nāma dvitīyaḥ samādhiḥ, sāṃbhogikaś ca kāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Thus the second <s>samādhi</s>, called <s>maṇḍalarājāgrī</s> ("foremost king of the maṇḍala"), and the <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment) body.

body.text: tato gaurīṃ caurīṃ yāvan maṇḍalādhipatiṃ pratyekam anupūrvyā daśasu dikṣu nirantaraṃ saṃsphārya, sattvānām arthaṃ kṛtvā, teṣv eva saṃhṛtya, kṛtakṛtyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ maṇḍalādhipatiṃ ca niṣprapañcasukhasamarpitaṃ paśyet. tatra gaurī kāyasya bhūtapratyavekṣāyāṃ sattvān vyavasthāpayati, caurī cittasya, vettālī vācaḥ, ghasmarī jñānasya, pukkasī kāyasya samyagjñāne, śabarī cittasya, caṇḍālī vācaḥ, ḍombī jñānasya. maṇḍaleśvaras tu mahāvajradharapade sattvān avasthāpayati.
body.translated_text: Then, having emanated <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Caurī</s>, and the rest, up to the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, individually and in sequence into the ten directions without interruption, and having accomplished the welfare of beings, one should withdraw [them] back into those very [places], and should visualize the <s>maṇḍala</s> as having fulfilled its purpose and the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s> as having been offered to the bliss free from conceptual elaboration (<s>niṣprapañcasukha</s>). Therein, <s>Gaurī</s> establishes beings in the true examination of body, <s>Caurī</s> of mind, <s>Vettālī</s> of speech, <s>Ghasmarī</s> of knowledge, <s>Pukkasī</s> in the correct knowledge of body, <s>Śabarī</s> of mind, <s>Caṇḍālī</s> of speech, <s>Ḍombī</s> of knowledge. The lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, however, establishes beings in the state of <s>Mahāvajradhara</s>.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ ṣaḍaṅgayogena samatāṃ bhāvayet.
body.translated_text: Immediately after that, one should cultivate equality (<s>samatā</s>) through the six-limbed yoga (<s>ṣaḍaṅgayoga</s>).

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ tataḥ pītaṃ harin nīlaṃ sitaṃ kramāt /
children.translated_text: Black, red, then yellow, green, blue, and white, in order,
And as the mere innate bliss (<s>sahajānanda</s>), one should meditate on the circle (<s>cakra</s>) together with its lord.

body.text: iti karmarājāgrī nāma tṛtīyaḥ samādhiḥ, nairmāṇikaś
body.translated_text: Thus the third <s>samādhi</s>, called <s>karmarājāgrī</s> ("foremost king of action"), and the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation)

body.text: ca kāyaḥ. bhāvanākhinno mantraṃ japet. samaṇḍalam ātmānaṃ devatārūpeṇāvirbhūtaṃ vicintya
body.translated_text: body. When fatigued from meditation, one should recite the <s>mantra</s>. Having visualized oneself as the <s>maṇḍala</s>, manifested in the form of the deity,

body.text: oṃ deva picuvajra hūṃ 3 phaṭ svāhā
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ deva picuvajra hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>

body.text: iti hṛtsūrye trayodaśa mantrākṣarāṇy ūrdhvaśiraskāni pradīpavaj jvalanti maṇḍalībhūtāni manasābhilikhya, tāny eva vācayan vajravācā krodhavācā vā japet. sarvamukhebhyaḥ sarvadevīmukhebhyaś ca mantram uccarantam adhimuñcet. iyataiva svadevatāyā aṣṭaguṇo jāpaḥ sarvadevīnāṃ ca mantrajāpaḥ kṛto bhavati.
body.translated_text: Thus, mentally inscribing the thirteen <s>mantra</s> syllables on the sun [disc] at the heart, blazing like a lamp with their heads upward, arranged in a circle, one should recite those very [syllables], uttering them with <s>vajra</s>-speech or wrathful speech. One should resolve that the <s>mantra</s> is being uttered from all mouths and from the mouths of all goddesses. By just this much, the eightfold <s>jāpa</s> (recitation) of one's own deity and the <s>mantra</s>-recitation of all the goddesses is accomplished.

body.text: tataḥ praṇidhānaṃ kuryāt.
body.translated_text: Then one should make the aspiration prayer (<s>praṇidhāna</s>):

children.translated_text: "The state of <s>Mahāvajradhṛt</s> (the Great Vajra-holder), which is the all-in-all of all <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: ebhir labheya kuśalair lambhayeyaṃ ca taj jagat //
children.translated_text: May I attain through these merits, and may I cause the world to attain it too.

children.text: caryā saṃbodhaye yā ca saṃbuddhānāṃ ca yā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The conduct (<s>caryā</s>) that leads to enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), and that which the fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s>

children.text: varṇitā bodhivajreṇa sā caryāstu dvayī mama //
children.translated_text: Have described through <s>Bodhivajra</s> — may that twofold conduct be mine."

body.text: tataḥ sanāyakaṃ maṇḍalaṃ pūrvavat saṃpūjya, svahṛnmantre devīr antarbhāvya, ādhāramaṇḍalam ativistīrṇam adhimucya,
body.translated_text: Then, having worshipped the <s>maṇḍala</s> together with its lord as before, having absorbed the goddesses into the <s>mantra</s> at one's own heart, having resolved upon the support-<s>maṇḍala</s> (<s>ādhāramaṇḍala</s>) as exceedingly vast,

body.text: catvāri mahābhūtāni pukkasyādisvabhāvāni niścitya, hevajrāhaṃkareṇotthāya tathaiva viharet. madhyāhnapradoṣasandhyayor dhyānagṛhaṃ praviśya pūrvavad ādhāramaṇḍalaṃ tanmadhyāsane cātmānaṃ samāpannāṣṭānanahevajrarūpaṃ jhaṭiti dṛṣṭvā, hṛdbījaniścāritāś ca devīr yathāsthānaṃ niveśya, sarvamaṇḍalam ānandamayaṃ dhyātvā, pūjāstutyamṛtāsvādaṃ jāpādikaṃ ca kuryāt. nidrākāle ṣaḍaṅgayogaṃ sahajānandayogaṃ vābhimukhīkṛtya supyāt. caturdevīgītisaṃcoditaś ca nidrāta uttiṣṭhet. utthāya sarvaṃ pūrvavat kuryāt. evaṃ pratyahaṃ yāvat siddhinimittāni paśyati. tāni dṛṣṭvā yathātantram abhimatasiddher upāyam anutiṣṭhed iti.
body.translated_text: having ascertained that the four great elements have the nature of <s>Pukkasī</s> and the others, one should rise with the self-identification as <s>Hevajra</s> and conduct oneself accordingly. At the junctures of midday and dusk, one should enter the meditation chamber and, as before, [visualize] the support-<s>maṇḍala</s>, and upon the seat in its center, instantly see oneself in the form of the eight-faced <s>Hevajra</s> in meditation, and having emanated the goddesses from the seed-syllable at the heart and placed them in their proper positions, and having meditated on the entire <s>maṇḍala</s> as pervaded by bliss, one should perform worship, praise, tasting of <s>amṛta</s>, recitation, and so forth. At the time of sleep, one should fall asleep facing the six-limbed yoga or the yoga of innate bliss (<s>sahajānandayoga</s>). And one should awaken from sleep, roused by the song of the four goddesses. Upon rising, one should perform everything as before. Thus, daily, until one sees the signs of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). Having seen those [signs], one should carry out the means for the desired <s>siddhi</s> according to the <s>tantra</s>.

body.text:
guruguṇadhanadhāmnaḥ sādhanaṃ herukasya
bhramaharam abhidhāya spaṣṭam aṣṭānanasya /
body.translated_text: Having clearly expounded the <s>sādhana</s> of <s>Heruka</s>, the eight-faced one, called <s>Bhramahara</s> ("Dispeller of Confusion"), [the work] of the guru who is an abode of qualities and wealth,

body.text: kuśalam idam avāptaṃ yan mayā janmabhājāṃ niravadhihitahetus tena vajrī jinaḥ syām //
body.translated_text: May the merit I have thus obtained, being the cause of boundless benefit for all born beings, make me a <s>Vajrī</s> (vajra-holder), a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror).
